title: Chapter 12: Agriculture & Major Crops of WB

blocks.content: West Bengal is one of the most productive agricultural states of India. It is the leading producer of rice, vegetables, and fish in the country.
Aman rice accounts for the largest share of total rice production in West Bengal, harvested mainly during the winter season.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: West Bengal is the leading producer of both Rice and Jute in India.
Aman rice (Winter rice) contributes the largest share to total rice output in the state.
Darjeeling Tea became the first Indian product to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2004.
The state features 6 distinct Agro-Climatic Zones ranging from Northern Hilly to Coastal Saline.
Burdwan (Bardhaman) district is traditionally known as the 'Rice Bowl of West Bengal'.
Aman rice is sown in June-July and harvested in November-December, constituting over 70% of state production.
Darjeeling Tea was granted India's first GI tag in the year 2004.
Purba Bardhaman is frequently asked in exams as the 'Rice Bowl of West Bengal' (Dhaner Gola).
Jute cultivation is heavily concentrated in Nadia, Murshidabad, North 24 Parganas, and Hooghly districts.

cells: WB is the largest producer of rice in India — main food crop; grown in all districts
WB is No. 1 producer in India; grown in Murshidabad, Nadia, North 24 Parganas
WB is 2nd largest producer; Darjeeling tea is GI-tagged and world-famous
WB is leading vegetable producer in India
North Bengal; Malda district famous for litchi
Malda & Murshidabad; Himsagar and Fazli mango — GI tagged
WB grows large amount of betel leaf
WB is top fish-producing state; Hilsa (Ilish) is state fish; Rohu, Katla also major
Murshidabad district produces large amount of Mulberry silk
[EXAM TIP] WB is India's No.1 producer of Rice, Jute, and Vegetables. For tea, WB is 2nd (after Assam). Darjeeling Tea has GI tag. These are asked every year in both SI and Constable exams.
